title: Temporal pinning and rotation for KV cache fragmentation mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Under continuous batching and variable sequence lengths our GPU KV cache exhibits long-tail fragmentation. Small recurrent allocations and uneven eviction patterns create many tiny free slots that hurt reuse and increase memory pressure, forcing conservative admission/batching settings and causing higher token cost or OOM risk.

Goal: Implement a low-overhead allocation strategy that lowers fragmentation exposure without large pause times or blocking the critical inference path. The approach should be compatible with streaming/continuous batching and maintain low tail latency. This ticket proposes a temporal pinning + rotation scheme that organizes KV storage into short-lived 'rotation epochs' and uses lightweight pinning for very-hot entries to reduce churn and micro-fragmentation.
proposal:
1) Partition KV address space into fixed-size chunks (chunk granularity tuned by model type) and maintain a small in-memory chunk metadata table.
2) Introduce temporal pinning: when a key is observed to be accessed repeatedly within a short window we mark its chunk as 'pinned' (fast path) to avoid moving it during background rotation. Pin duration is adaptive based on access rate and token-span.
3) Rotation epochs: in the background, non-pinned chunks are eligible for rotation where fragmented chunks are compacted into contiguous destination chunks by a background mover. Rotation is incremental and rate-limited to avoid impacting inference.
4) Eviction lanes: keep multiple eviction lanes (hot, warm, cold) to classify chunks by access recency; eviction selects from cold lanes first and skips pinned chunks.
5) Fragmentation signal: compute a lightweight fragmentation score per chunk (free-run-length histogram + occupancy ratio). Triggers for rotation/merge are based on per-GPU budget and fragmentation score thresholds.
6) Integrate with batching: allocator exposes a non-blocking fast-path for allocate/free and defers complex compaction work to the background mover. Batches can annotate expected KV live-span to influence pin policy.
7) Fallbacks: If rotation budget is exhausted or OOM imminent, fallback to aggressive eviction policies and partial drops of cold chunks with metrics annotated for postmortem.
architecture_changes: New components: chunk metadata table (per-GPU), rotation controller (global-per-node with per-GPU workers), background mover thread per GPU, pin manager integrated into fast allocator, fragmentation telemetry exporter. Modify allocator API to accept optional expected_lifetime_hint for allocations. Require small changes to batching layer to propagate lifetime hints and access counts.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation score (95th percentile across synthetic mixed-length workload) reduced by >= 40% in lab runs compared to baseline allocator
Tail latency (99.9th) for streaming requests not increased by more than 5% under normal rotation budget
Background rotation uses <= 7% additional GPU memory bandwidth and safe-limits set to avoid affecting inference kernels
No new OOMs introduced in canary on dedicated pool for 72h under representative traffic
Telemetry visible in Console: chunk fragmentation distribution, rotation throughput, pin hit-rate, eviction lane sizes
telemetry_and_metrics: pin hit-rate and average pin duration
OOM/eviction events annotated with rotation budget state
rollout_plan: 1) Run simulator tests and microbenchmarks (local) to tune chunk size and pin thresholds
2) Internal cluster canary (single node, non-customer traffic) for 24-48h to validate micro-impact
3) Dedicated customer canary (low-traffic tenant) for 72h with extended metrics collection
4) Gradual ramp to 20% of dedicated pools with rollback switches: disable rotation, disable pinning, enforce conservative allocator
5) Full rollout to runtime-2.4 after 7d of stable canaries and SRE sign-off
implementation_steps: A. Simulation harness: model mixed sequence-length workloads and fragmentation; iterate on chunk size and pin heuristics
B. Implement chunk metadata table and fast-path hooks in allocator (no blocking allocations)
C. Implement pin manager that consumes access stream and exposes pin/unpin APIs
D. Implement background mover and rotation controller with rate limiting and safety checks
E. Instrument telemetry and add Console dashboards for fragmentation signals
F. Add integration tests covering edge cases: rapid churn, large allocations, slow mover, forced OOM
G. Canary rollout and profile memory bandwidth, latency, and rotation behavior
H. Iterate on thresholds and implement adaptive budgeter that scales rotation based on observed tail latency
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for chunk metadata operations and pin lifecycle
Fuzz tests of concurrent allocate/free/pin/unpin with background mover enabled
End-to-end perf tests: synthetic mixed-length, heavy-churn, and long-seq streaming workloads
Back-to-back OOM injection tests to ensure safe fallbacks and proper metrics
Comparative run against baseline allocator to produce CI perf artifact (latency/cost/fragmentation)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Background rotation competes for GPU memory bandwidth and impacts inference kernels. Mitigation: strict rate limiter and bandwidth-aware mover that yields to inference scheduler.
Risk: Pin misclassification keeps fragmented chunks pinned and prevents healing. Mitigation: max pin duration and decaying pin strength; require multiple access confirmations for long pins.
Risk: Complexity increases bug surface around concurrent moves. Mitigation: phased rollout, heavy fuzz and formalized acquisition order for chunk locks, and opt-in safety flags in canary.
Risk: Heuristics tuned to one workload generalize poorly. Mitigation: expose tuning knobs and automatic telemetry-driven recommendations in Optimize product later.

2026-02-20 - Samir Gupta: Reviewed and requested clearer safe-fallback semantics; suggested adding explicit bandwidth limits for the mover and an emergency 'freeze-rotation' flag that SRE can toggle.
2026-02-22 - Miguel Alvarez: Implemented chunk metadata prototype and allocator fast-path hooks. Microbenchmarks show fast-path latency unchanged within noise (p99 delta +0.8%).
2026-02-25 - Priya Menon (SRE): Asked for canary checklist and observability requirements; added dashboard panels and alert thresholds for rotation-throughput drop and pin-saturation.

2026-02-28 - Miguel Alvarez: Background mover integrated and running in dev cluster; observed rotation uses ~4% extra memory bandwidth at default rate. Identified a race in concurrent move + eviction, added locking ordering to the design and added tests.
